audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for sign demand, yeast of Pharisees/Sadducees, Peter confession, rock/keys/binding-loosing, first passion prediction, Satan/adversary rebuke, cross-following, psyche life/soul, Son of Humanity coming.

verses.restored: Pharisees and Sadducees came, testing him, and asked him to show them a sign from heaven.

familiar.text: The Pharisees also with the Sadducees came, and tempting desired him that he would shew them a sign from heaven.

modern.text: Then the Pharisees and Sadducees came and tested Jesus by asking Him to show them a sign from heaven.

original.text: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ Σαδδουκαῖοι πειράζοντες ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν σημεῖον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπιδεῖξαι αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: He answered them, When evening comes you say, Fair weather, for the sky is red.

familiar.text: He answered and said unto them, When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red.

modern.text: But He replied, “When evening comes, you say, ‘The weather will be fair, for the sky is red,’

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· ⸂Ὀψίας γενομένης λέγετε· Εὐδία, πυρράζει γὰρ ὁ οὐρανός·

verses.restored: And in the morning, Storm today, for the sky is red and gloomy. You know how to discern the face of the sky, but not the signs of the times.

familiar.text: And in the morning, It will be foul weather to day: for the sky is red and lowring. O ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times?

modern.text: and in the morning, ‘Today it will be stormy, for the sky is red and overcast.’ You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky, but not the signs of the times.

original.text: καὶ πρωΐ· Σήμερον χειμών, πυρράζει γὰρ στυγνάζων ὁ οὐρανός. ⸀τὸ μὲν πρόσωπον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γινώσκετε διακρίνειν, τὰ δὲ σημεῖα τῶν καιρῶν οὐ δύνασθε.⸃

verses.restored: A harmful and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given except the sign of Jonah. Leaving them, he went away.

familiar.text: A wicked and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given unto it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas. And he left them, and departed.

modern.text: A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.” Then He left them and went away. The Leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees (Mark 8:14–21; Luke 12:1–3)

original.text: Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον ⸀Ἰωνᾶ. καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἀπῆλθεν.

verses.restored: The disciples came to the other side and had forgotten to take bread.

familiar.text: And when his disciples were come to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread.

modern.text: When they crossed to the other side, the disciples forgot to take bread.

original.text: Καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ εἰς τὸ πέραν ἐπελάθοντο ἄρτους λαβεῖν.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, Watch and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

familiar.text: Then Jesus said unto them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

modern.text: “Watch out!” Jesus told them. “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.

verses.restored: They reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we took no bread.

familiar.text: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have taken no bread.

modern.text: They discussed this among themselves and concluded, “It is because we did not bring any bread.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄρτους οὐκ ἐλάβομεν.

verses.restored: Knowing this, Jesus said, Ones of little trust, why do you reason among yourselves that you have no bread?

familiar.text: Which when Jesus perceived, he said unto them, O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves, because ye have brought no bread?

modern.text: Aware of their conversation, Jesus said, “You of little faith, why are you debating among yourselves about having no bread?

original.text: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸀εἶπεν· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, ὀλιγόπιστοι, ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ⸀ἐλάβετε;

verses.restored: Do you not yet understand or remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?

familiar.text: Do ye not yet understand, neither remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?

modern.text: Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?

original.text: οὔπω νοεῖτε, οὐδὲ μνημονεύετε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους τῶν πεντακισχιλίων καὶ πόσους κοφίνους ἐλάβετε;

verses.restored: Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you took up?

familiar.text: Neither the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?

modern.text: Or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?

original.text: οὐδὲ τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους τῶν τετρακισχιλίων καὶ πόσας σπυρίδας ἐλάβετε;

verses.restored: How do you not understand that I did not speak to you about bread, but to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees?

familiar.text: How is it that ye do not understand that I spake it not to you concerning bread, that ye should beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees?

modern.text: How do you not understand that I was not telling you about bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

original.text: πῶς οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι οὐ περὶ ⸀ἄρτων εἶπον ὑμῖν; ⸂προσέχετε δὲ⸃ ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.

verses.restored: Then they understood that he did not say to beware of bread-leaven, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

familiar.text: Then understood they how that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

modern.text: Then they understood that He was not telling them to beware of the leaven used in bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees. Peter’s Confession of Christ (Mark 8:27–30; Luke 9:18–20; John 6:67–71)

original.text: τότε συνῆκαν ὅτι οὐκ εἶπεν προσέχειν ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης ⸂τῶν ἄρτων⸃ ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ τῆς διδαχῆς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων.

verses.restored: Coming into the region of Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asked his disciples, Who do people say the Son of Humanity is?

familiar.text: When Jesus came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?

modern.text: When Jesus came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, He questioned His disciples: “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”

original.text: Ἐλθὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὰ μέρη Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου ἠρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων· ⸀Τίνα λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου;

verses.restored: They said, Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.

familiar.text: And they said, Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets.

modern.text: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οἱ μὲν Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν, ἕτεροι δὲ Ἰερεμίαν ἢ ἕνα τῶν προφητῶν.

verses.restored: He said to them, But you, who do you say I am?

familiar.text: He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am?

modern.text: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?”

original.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι;

verses.restored: Simon Peter answered, You are the Messiah, the Son of the living Divine.

familiar.text: And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.

modern.text: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος εἶπεν· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος.

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, Blessed/flourishing are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father in the heavens.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.

modern.text: Jesus replied, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! For this was not revealed to you by flesh and blood, but by My Father in heaven.

original.text: ⸂ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ⸃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακάριος εἶ, Σίμων Βαριωνᾶ, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα οὐκ ἀπεκάλυψέν σοι ἀλλʼ ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·

verses.restored: And I also say to you that you are Peter/Rock, and on this rock I will build my assembly, and the gates of Hades will not overpower it.

familiar.text: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

modern.text: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.

original.text: κἀγὼ δέ σοι λέγω ὅτι σὺ εἶ Πέτρος, καὶ ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ οἰκοδομήσω μου τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, καὶ πύλαι ᾅδου οὐ κατισχύσουσιν αὐτῆς·

verses.restored: I will give you the keys of the reign of the heavens; whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in the heavens.

familiar.text: And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

modern.text: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.”

original.text: ⸀δώσω σοι τὰς ⸀κλεῖδας τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, καὶ ὃ ⸀ἐὰν δήσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, καὶ ὃ ⸁ἐὰν λύσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

verses.restored: Then he ordered the disciples to tell no one that he was the Messiah.

familiar.text: Then charged he his disciples that they should tell no man that he was Jesus the Christ.

modern.text: Then He admonished the disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ. Christ’s Passion Foretold (Mark 8:31–33; Luke 9:21–22)

original.text: τότε ⸀διεστείλατο τοῖς ⸀μαθηταῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ εἴπωσιν ὅτι αὐτός ⸀ἐστιν ὁ χριστός.

verses.restored: From then Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and on the third day be raised.

familiar.text: From that time forth began Jesus to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.

modern.text: From that time on Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.

original.text: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ⸂ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ δεικνύειν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν ⸂εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπελθεῖν⸃ καὶ πολλὰ παθεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθῆναι.

verses.restored: Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying, Mercy to you, Lord; this shall never happen to you.

familiar.text: Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.

modern.text: Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him. “Far be it from You, Lord!” he said. “This shall never happen to You!”

original.text: καὶ προσλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ὁ Πέτρος ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἵλεώς σοι, κύριε· οὐ μὴ ἔσται σοι τοῦτο.

verses.restored: But turning, he said to Peter, Go behind me, adversary; you are a stumbling-block to me, because you are not thinking the things of the Divine, but the things of humans.

familiar.text: But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.

modern.text: But Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me. For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.” Take Up Your Cross (Mark 8:34–38; Luke 9:23–27)

original.text: ὁ δὲ στραφεὶς εἶπεν τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ· σκάνδαλον ⸂εἶ ἐμοῦ⸃, ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

verses.restored: Then Jesus said to his disciples, If anyone wants to come after me, let that one deny self, take up the cross, and follow me.

familiar.text: Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

modern.text: Then Jesus told His disciples, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.

original.text: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἐλθεῖν, ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.

verses.restored: For whoever wants to save his life/soul will lose it, but whoever loses his life/soul because of me will find it.

familiar.text: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it.

modern.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.

original.text: ὃς γὰρ ⸀ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δʼ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν.

verses.restored: For what will a person be profited if gaining the whole world but forfeiting his life/soul? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life/soul?

familiar.text: For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

modern.text: What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?

original.text: τί γὰρ ⸀ὠφεληθήσεται ἄνθρωπος ἐὰν τὸν κόσμον ὅλον κερδήσῃ τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ζημιωθῇ; ἢ τί δώσει ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ;

verses.restored: For the Son of Humanity is about to come in the glory of his Father with his messengers, and then he will give back to each according to practice.

familiar.text: For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.

modern.text: For the Son of Man will come in His Father’s glory with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to what he has done.

original.text: μέλλει γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ, καὶ τότε ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: there are some standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the Son of Humanity coming in his reign.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.

modern.text: Truly I tell you, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom.”

original.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ⸀ὅτι εἰσίν τινες ⸂τῶν ὧδε ἑστώτων⸃ οἵτινες οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ.
